summary: A note from the University of Illinois on making mathematical software libraries available over the ARPANET. It lists projects such as the Bell Labs library, IMSL and NATS, and suggests that the network could make such libraries shareable resources. It discusses what stands in the way.

eli5.summary: Many places had collections of ready-made math tools. This note says the network could let everyone borrow them instead of building their own.

questions: sharing math libraries over a network
subtitle: A proposal to make mathematical software libraries available as a shared network resource.

tldr.problem: Mathematical and statistical software libraries existed in various places (Bell Labs, IMSL, NATS), but were not easily shared across the ARPANET.
tldr.mechanism: The memo suggests that the ARPANET could enhance the value of these libraries by making them accessible to all networked sites, even though different installations need different software and have different preferences.
tldr.outcome: The University of Illinois planned to obtain the NATS library and make it available on several network IBM/360-370s and PDP-10s, and invited others to share their experiences with mathematical software.

today: RFC 382 is Unknown status. It is a historical proposal for network-wide software sharing from 1972. Modern software distribution via package managers and cloud platforms has realized this vision.

sections.title: The Opportunity
sections.content: Lawrence McDaniel of the University of Illinois notes that several organizations had developed high-quality libraries of mathematical and statistical subroutines. The Bell Laboratories had a numerical mathematics program library, IMSL Inc. offered their IMSL Library I, and a joint project between the National Science Foundation, Argonne Laboratories, Stanford and Texas had developed the Wilkinson linear algebra routines under the NATS project.
sections.eli5: Several big institutions have built libraries of math tools. Bell Labs, IMSL, and Stanford-Argonne each made ones.

sections.title: Sharing Libraries Over the Network
sections.content: The memo argues that the ARPANET could enhance the value of these libraries as a sharable network resource. Although different sites have different mathematical software needs and personal software preferences, everyone could benefit from information exchange about mathematical software of interest.
sections.eli5: The network could let researchers use each other's math tools. Even though every place has its own favorites, sharing would help everyone.

sections.title: The University of Illinois Plan
sections.content: McDaniel indicates that the University of Illinois planned to obtain the NATS library and, with the project's cooperation, intended to make it available on several network IBM/360-370 and PDP-10 computers. Interested parties could contact Lawrence McDaniel via the NIC (identifier LM) or by telephone at (217) 333-8497.
sections.eli5: The University of Illinois wants to get the NATS math library and put it on computers people can reach over the network. They invited others to join.
